text: Le match a basculé après la mi-temps quand Seabrook Town a marqué 4 buts entre la 53e et la 90+3e minute, renversant un déficit de 2-0 pour s'imposer 4-2 [#1104] [#1448] [#1882] [#1906]. Harbour City a dominé la première mi-temps avec un jeu patient et un bon xG de 0.75 (signifiant des chances assez nettes pour marquer), mais le carton rouge de Joon Whitfield à la 43e minute a compliqué leur défense [#871] [#905]. Marek Barros, star du match, a brillé avec un but, 2 passes décisives et une grande activité défensive (9 interceptions). Seabrook Town a joué un pressing plus haut à partir de la 65e minute, jouant plus vite et plus direct, ce qui leur a permis de gagner plus de ballons et d’attaquer rapidement, notamment grâce à leurs buts sur contre-attaque en fin de match [#1361] [#1882] [#1906]. Leur supériorité est confirmée par un xG total de 3.48, ce qui signifie qu'ils ont eu plus que trois fois plus d’occasions nettes que Harbour City (xG 1.0).

trace.output: Brief: full-match recap for fan audience in fr

- Seabrook Town scored the last 4 goals from 53' to 90+3', turning a 2-0 deficit into a 4-2 victory. [#1104, #1448, #1882, #1906]
- Harbour City's Marek Barros was the player of the match with 1 goal, 2 assists, 4 tackles, 9 interceptions and a 9.8 rating. [No single evidence ID for summary]
- Harbour City had a first half xG of 0.75 but only managed 1 goal before going down 0-2 early in second half. [#905, #975]
- Seabrook Town had a stronger overall xG of 3.48 and more shots (22) than Harbour City (10). [No single evidence ID for summary]
- Red card for Harbour City's Joon Whitfield at 43' likely impacted their defensive capability. [#871]

- Seabrook Town capitalized on quick ball recoveries to initiate rapid attacks, as seen in Tariq Marlowe's goal at 53', which came from a very short build-up starting immediately from a regain with no passes before shooting [#1104]. This reflects their tendency to press and transition directly.

- Their switching to a higher press and more direct play around the 65th minute (press increased from 0.66 to 0.84, directness from 0.42 to 0.57, line height from 0.6 to 0.72) was a tactical response to chase the game, increasing chances and pace significantly in the second half [#1361]. This aligns with their 3-4-3 formation and wide crossing style, exploiting width and pressing to regain possession quickly.

- Harbour City's goals came from patient, build-up play consistent with their 4-2-3-1 formation and patient short passing style: Elias Okafor’s goal involved a 17-pass sequence over nearly a minute showing patient buildup before a through ball assist by Barros [#905], while Barros’s second goal involved a cross after a corner, indicating utilization of set pieces despite an overall short-passing style [#975].

- Marek Barros notably contributed both defensively and offensively, with 4 tackles, 9 interceptions, 5 key passes, 2 assists, and a goal, highlighting how Harbour City relied on a technically skilled attacking midfielder to create and win the ball back, fitting their tactical profile [player_of_the_match].

- Seabrook Town’s late goals, including two from Kian Romano in stoppage time, resulted from quick transitions and through passes following ball regains (one counter-attack scenario at 90+2 minutes), showing effective exploitation of disorganized defense during Harbour City’s pressing attempts when chasing the game [#1882, #1906].

- The overall stats reflect Seabrook Town’s dominance in possession (53.4%), shots (22), and especially higher xG (3.48 vs 1.0), consistent with their aggressive, wide, crossing style and formation that favors offensive overloads and pressing traps to regain possession and quickly create chances.
